narrative.heading: The busywork is the bottleneck
paragraphs: Most teams we meet aren't short on tools. They're short on connective tissue. Leads sit in a form for two days before anyone calls. The CRM is half-filled because updating it is a chore. Someone rebuilds the same report every Monday morning. Marketing can't tell which campaigns produced revenue, so budget gets set on instinct.
None of that is a technology problem. It's an integration and design problem — the kind that quietly costs you deals every month without ever becoming urgent enough to fix.
That's the work we do. We get the ERP and data foundations right, automate the manual work around them, then put AI on top. Skipping to the last step is why most AI projects stall.

faq.a: Usually a VP of Sales, a COO, or a founder who realises their team is spending too much time moving data between systems. They have revenue goals to hit and know that hiring more people to do manual data entry won't scale.

faq.q: Do you only work with Oracle and specific cloud vendors?
faq.a: No. We work across the modern stack. We frequently build on top of HubSpot, Salesforce, Snowflake, Databricks, AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud, connecting them via tools like Make, Zapier, or custom APIs. We focus on the business outcome, not forcing a specific vendor.

Most initial engagements take between 4 and 8 weeks to get into production. We prefer shipping small, highly valuable automations quickly rather than spending six months building a monolithic system before you see value.

faq.q: How do you protect proprietary data with AI?
faq.a: Yes. We never train public models on your proprietary data. We use enterprise-grade endpoints and architectures (like Retrieval-Augmented Generation) where your data stays within your tenant boundary and respects your existing permission models.
